rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.e1: You already know direct opposition. Now the kings are not on the same file.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.e2: For the pawn on e3, the key squares are d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.e3: Your king wants to reach one of them; the black king wants e6, from where it controls all three.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! Your king advances and stands on a diagonal with the black king.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to f4, on a diagonal with the black king.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3e2.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3e2.2: The black king goes to e6 and controls d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3f2.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3f2.2: The black king goes to e6 and controls d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3g2.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3g2.2: The black king goes to e6 and controls d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3g3.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3g3.2: The black king goes to e6 and controls d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3g4.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3g4.2: The black king goes to e6 and controls d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3e4.1: With that move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.f3e4.2: The black king goes to e6 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to Black.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.e3e4.1: Pushing the pawn now does not win: Black can draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.err.e3e4.2: With the pawn on e4, the key squares move up to d6, e6 and f6, and the black king takes e6.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always closes the way.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always closes the way.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l1: Notice: the kings are on the same diagonal, with just one square between them, e5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l2: This is called diagonal opposition. As with direct opposition, the side that has just moved has it: here, White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l3: Black takes the king to e6 and controls d5, e5 and f5.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l4: You face it from e4: the diagonal opposition becomes direct opposition, and it is still yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l5: The black king must give way: wherever it goes, your king gets into a key square.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king goes to d6.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l7: Your king gets into f5, a key square. The pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l8: Now imagine that, instead of taking the king to e4, White pushes the pawn.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l9: The black king goes to f6 and faces yours: now the direct opposition belongs to Black.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l10: It is a draw. Pushing the pawn early gave away the opposition: the king goes first, the pawn afterwards.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l11: Now let's go back to the position after the first move.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l12: What if Black takes the king to d5, close to the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l13: Your king gets into f5, a key square: once there, White wins, whatever the black king does.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l14: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l15: Keep the idea: with the kings on a diagonal and one square between them, the opposition belongs to the side that has just moved.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex1.l16: Now let's see the defence: Black can use the diagonal opposition too.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e1: Now you play Black, and the board turns around.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e2: The white king wants to reach d5, e5 or f5, the pawn's key squares.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.e3: Your king must close that path, and the means is the same as in attack: winning the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! Now the diagonal opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to e6, on a diagonal with the white king: the opposition passes to Black.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.1: This move loses: now White can win.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.2: The white king gets into f5, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7d7.1: This move loses: now White can win.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7d7.2: The white king gets into f5, a key square, and the pawn will promote.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7e8.2: The white king gets into f5, a key square, and the pawn will promote.

rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7f6.1: This move loses: now White can win.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.err.e7f6.2: The white king goes to f4 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.coroa: The pawn promoted. Without the opposition, Black cannot hold.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.capturado: The pawn fell: your king won the fight for the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: The black king was stalemated: stalemate is a draw, and the defence held.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l1: The kings are on the same diagonal, with one square between them, f5, and you have just moved: the opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king goes to f4, next to the key squares.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l3: You face it from f6: the diagonal opposition becomes direct, and it is still yours.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l4: The white king must give way, and your king keeps guarding the key squares. It is a draw.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l5: Now let's go back to the position with the white king on f4.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l6: What if, instead of facing it, your king goes to d5 to attack the pawn?
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l7: The white king gets into f5, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l8: Let's go back to the position with your king on e6.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.l9: That is why, against the king on f4, the answer is f6: facing it, keeping the opposition.
rot.diagonal.ideia.ex2.ponte: Now I play both sides in two positions. See who wins the opposition and if the attacker gets a key square.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.1: First position: the pawn is on c2, and the key squares are b4, c4 and d4.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.2: Your king goes to d3, on a diagonal with the black king, with one square between them: c4.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.3: You have just moved: the diagonal opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.4: The black king goes to c5 and controls b4, c4 and d4.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.5: Your king faces it from c3: direct opposition, and the black king must give way.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.6: The black king goes to b5.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.7: Your king gets into d4, a key square. The pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.8: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.9: What if the white king goes straight to c3, on the pawn's file?
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.10: The black king goes to c5 and faces it: the direct opposition belongs to Black, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.demos.outraAla.11: Let's go back to the starting position. With the kings on a diagonal, leave one square between them after your move.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.1: Second position, now from Black's side, and the board has turned around.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.2: The pawn is on d2, and the key squares are c4, d4 and e4.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.3: Your king goes to d5, on a diagonal with the white king, with one square between them: c4. The opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.4: The white king goes to c3.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.5: You face it from c5: direct opposition. The white king cannot reach the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.6: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.7: What if your king goes straight to c5, toward the white king?
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.8: The white king faces it from c3: the direct opposition belongs to White, and White wins.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.9: Let's go back to the starting position.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.10: In defence the diagonal works too: after your move, one square between the kings, and the opposition is yours.
rot.diagonal.demos.defesa.ponte: Your turn: one attack and one defence against the machine. Look for the opposition on the diagonal too.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3d2.1: Going to d2, your king retreats away from the key squares e5, f5 and g5: the win slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3d2.2: The black king goes to f6 and controls e5, f5 and g5 before yours gets there.

rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3e2.2: The black king goes to f6 and controls e5, f5 and g5 before yours gets there.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3f2.1: Going to f2, your king retreats away from the key squares e5, f5 and g5: the win slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3f2.2: The black king goes to f6 and controls e5, f5 and g5 before yours gets there.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3d3.1: Going to d3, your king moves away from the pawn and does not take the opposition: the win slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3d3.2: The black king goes to f6 and controls e5, f5 and g5 before yours gets there.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3d4.1: Going to d4, your king advances but stays off the black king's diagonal: the win slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3d4.2: The black king goes to f6 and controls e5, f5 and g5 before yours gets there.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3f4.1: Going to f4, your king advances off the black king's diagonal and does not take the opposition: the win slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.e3f4.2: The black king goes to f6 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to Black.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.1: With the pawn on f4 before the king, the key squares move up to e6, f6 and g6: the win slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.err.f3f4.2: The black king goes to f6 and guards the new key squares; your king is far from them.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.diagonal.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king took the opposition on the diagonal and reached a key square.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6b5.1: Going to b5, your king leaves the white king's diagonal and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6b5.2: The white king goes to d4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6b6.1: Going to b6, your king moves away from the white king and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6b6.2: The white king goes to d4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6b7.1: Going to b7, your king retreats and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6b7.2: The white king goes to d4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6c7.1: Going to c7, your king retreats and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6c7.2: The white king goes to d4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6d7.1: Going to d7, your king retreats and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6d7.2: The white king goes to d4, a key square, and the pawn will promote.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6d6.1: Going to d6, your king stays off the white king's diagonal and does not take the opposition: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6d6.2: The white king goes to d4, a key square, and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6d5.1: Going to d5, your king goes too far and stays off the white king's diagonal: the draw slips away.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.err.c6d5.2: The white king goes to d3 and faces yours: the direct opposition belongs to White.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.diagonal.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king took the opposition on the diagonal and did not let the white king through.
